\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS11-P2-PHY-S1-Q03, source={TOAS - Test 11 (27 Jun 2022)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=multi, subtopic={Ohm's law}, answer={C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: resistance of a half cylindrical conductor | steps: current flows along the arc between the rectangular faces; resistance by integrating over radius; current and potential direction | I: integrate over the radial elements}]

The inner and outer radii of the cylinder are $a$ and $b$ respectively and the height of the cylinder is $h$. A potential difference $V$ is applied across the two rectangular faces of the conductor using a cell of emf $V$. \bfig{123.9}{TOAS11_p2_phy_s1_q03_1.png}

\opt{B}{Current flowing through the cell is $\dfrac{V\,(b-a)\,h}{\rho\pi b}$.}
\opt{C}{Current flowing through the cell is $\dfrac{V\cdot h\cdot\ln\left(\frac ba\right)}{\rho\cdot\pi}$.}
\opt{D}{Outer cylindrical surface is at a lower voltage than the inner surface.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
